key_insight: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization (Ranking-PE) swaps accuracy-based scoring for pairwise ranking so prompt evolution optimizes AUROC instead of class-balance-sensitive correctness.
clinical_relevance: In imbalanced clinical diagnosis, this can better prioritize true risk ranking from multimodal models, which is more useful than raw accuracy for screening and triage.
method: Replaced binary per-example correctness with pairwise positive-vs-negative ordering in the prompt search score matrix.
Used the same ranking signal for Pareto dominance, reflection feedback, and final prompt selection.
Kept the process model-call efficient, with no extra evaluations or surrogate loss.
evidence_signal: Across three MIMIC diseases, Ranking-PE improved AUROC over accuracy-based prompt evolution by +5.8 points on fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B and +16.2 points on MedGemma-4B.
watch_item: Results depend on a strong medical visual backbone, so prompt search cannot fully compensate for weak multimodal pretraining or vision tuning.
paper_title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
